title: MACD and Stochastic
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/0/body: **MACD** (Moving Average Convergence Divergence) is built from **the difference between two EMAs**: **MACD line = EMA 12 − EMA 26**. When the fast average pulls away from the slow one, MACD grows, meaning momentum is stronger.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/1/body: The **signal line** = an EMA 9 of the MACD line itself. The **histogram** = MACD − signal, the gap between those two lines drawn as bars. The standard setting: **12, 26, 9**.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/1/tip: This app's charts don't draw MACD, so we'll practice it here with numbers and scenarios.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/2/prompt: Bitcoin's EMA 12 is $61,500 and its EMA 26 is $62,000. What's the MACD line, and what does it mean?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/2/option: −500: the fast MA is below the slow one
+500: the fast MA is above the slow one
−500: the fast MA is above the slow one
123,500: the sum of the two MAs
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/2/explan: 61,500 − 62,000 = −500. A negative MACD means the EMA 12 is below the EMA 26 and short-term momentum is bearish.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/3/prompt: Price has been in this steady uptrend for a long time. Where is the MACD line (12, 26, 9) most likely right now?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/3/option: Above zero, since EMA 12 is above EMA 26
Below zero, since EMA 12 is below EMA 26
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/3/explan: In a steady uptrend, the fast average sits above the slow one, so their difference is positive. MACD has no 70 level or overbought zone; that's RSI.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/4/prompt: The MACD line is at 15 pips and the signal line is at 10 pips. What's the histogram?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/4/explan: Histogram = MACD − signal = 15 − 10 = 5 pips. Positive means the MACD line is above the signal line.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/5/statem: Like RSI, MACD moves between 0 and 100.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/5/explan: MACD has no fixed range. It's the difference between two averages, expressed in price units, so it can be any positive or negative number.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/6/body: When MACD pulls away from the signal line, the bars get **taller**. When the positive bars get **shorter** one after another, the MACD line is closing in on the signal line and bullish momentum is fading. You often see this **before a cross**.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/7/prompt: The MACD histogram over the last 4 candles was +8, +6, +3, +1. What's a sensible read?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/7/option: Bullish momentum is fading and a bearish cross is near
The MACD line has dropped below zero
Price will surely drop on the next candle
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/7/explan: The bars are still positive but shrinking, so MACD is closing in on the signal line. It's an early warning, not a certainty.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/8/senten: The MACD line is the difference between the EMA ___ and the EMA ___.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/8/explan: MACD = EMA 12 − EMA 26. The 9 belongs to the signal line, which is an EMA 9 of the MACD itself.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/9/prompt: Put the steps for building MACD in order.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/9/items/: EMA 9 of the MACD line = signal line
lessons/oscillators-u2-l1/steps/9/explan: Each part is built from the one before: first the two EMAs, then their difference, then an average of that difference, and finally the gap between those two.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/0/body: The **Stochastic** asks: where is the current close **within the range of the last 14 candles**? **%K = (close − lowest low) ÷ (highest high − lowest low) × 100**. Near 100 means near the top of the range; near 0 means near the bottom.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/1/body: In the **Slow Stochastic** with the **14, 3, 3** setting, the %K line is smoothed with a 3-candle average, and **%D** is a 3-candle average of that %K. Above **80** counts as overbought and below **20** as oversold.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/1/tip: Like MACD, the Stochastic isn't drawn on this app's charts. We'll give you its values in the questions.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/2/prompt: Over Bitcoin's last 14 candles, the highest high was $64,000 and the lowest low was $60,000. Price closed at $61,000. What's the raw %K?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/3/prompt: If price closes exactly at the highest high of the last 14 candles, what's the raw %K?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/3/explan: The top of the fraction (close − low) equals the bottom (high − low), so %K = 100. A close at the lowest low gives %K = 0.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/4/statem: The Stochastic is usually more sensitive than RSI and gives more signals (and more false ones).
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/4/explan: The Stochastic only measures where price sits in its recent range and jumps quickly between 0 and 100. That's why its signals are more frequent but noisier.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/5/body: The most common signal is **a %K/%D cross in an extreme zone**: %K crossing above %D while both are below 20 (a possible bounce up), or crossing below it while both are above 80. These signals work best in a **ranging market**.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/5/tip: In a strong trend, the Stochastic can stay above 80 or below 20 for a long time.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/6/prompt: The market is ranging and price has reached the bottom of the range. The Stochastic (14, 3, 3) is below 20, and on the last candle %K crossed above %D. What's more likely?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/6/explan: The range bottom has turned price back before, the last candle is strongly bullish, and the Stochastic's bullish cross happened in oversold territory. A move back toward the middle of the range is more likely. Stop loss below the low.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/7/pairs/: Where the close sits in the 14-candle range
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/8/prompt: In a strong uptrend, the Stochastic has stayed above 80 for 6 candles. What's the best read?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/8/option: The trend is strong; overbought alone isn't a reason to sell
Sell right away because it's above 80
The indicator is broken and needs replacing
A bearish divergence must have formed
lessons/oscillators-u2-l2/steps/8/explan: The Stochastic shows where price sits in its recent range. In a strong trend, price keeps closing near the top of the range, so staying above 80 is natural.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/0/body: When the **MACD line crosses above the signal line**, it counts as a **bullish signal**, and when it crosses below, a **bearish signal**. At that exact moment, the **histogram flips sign**, from negative to positive or the other way around.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/1/body: When **MACD moves above zero**, the **EMA 12 has moved above the EMA 26**: a slower but firmer confirmation of a trend change. Many traders see a bullish cross **above zero** as a sign the uptrend is continuing, and a bullish cross **below zero** as an early (and riskier) reversal signal.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/2/prompt: The MACD line went from below zero to above zero. What does that mean?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/2/option: The EMA 12 moved above the EMA 26
Price closed above the Bollinger Band
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/2/explan: MACD = EMA 12 − EMA 26. When that difference goes from negative to positive, the fast average has crossed above the slow one.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/3/statem: When the MACD histogram flips from negative to positive, the MACD line has crossed above the signal line.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/3/explan: Histogram = MACD − signal. Turning positive means MACD is now bigger than the signal line: a bullish cross.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/4/prompt: After a price low, in what order do these usually happen?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/4/items/: MACD crosses above the signal line
The MACD line crosses above zero
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/4/explan: The histogram is the fastest part and reacts first. Then the signal line cross happens, and the zero-line cross (the EMA 12/26 cross) comes last.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/5/prompt: It's an uptrend, and after a pullback, price has rallied strongly again. MACD just crossed above the signal line, above the zero line. What's next?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/5/explan: A bullish cross above zero means momentum is back in line with the main trend after the pullback. Many traders read this as a trend continuation signal. Stop loss below the pullback low; crosses can fail too.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/6/body: Since MACD is built from moving averages, it gets **whipsawed** in a **ranging market** just like MA crossovers: the MACD line swings around zero and gives cross after cross. Combining it with **key levels** and the **higher-timeframe trend** improves signal quality.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/7/prompt: On the EUR/USD daily, price is above the 200 MA. On the 4-hour, price is at a previous support, MACD crossed above the signal line below zero, and the Stochastic has turned up from below 20. What's the most sensible read?
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/7/option: Several clues agree: buy on confirmation, stop below support
Sell, since MACD is still below zero
Do nothing; indicators are always wrong
Buy with your whole account since everything is bullish
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/7/explan: The long-term trend, support, the early MACD cross and the Stochastic turning up all point the same way. It's still about probability, so use sensible size and a stop loss.
lessons/oscillators-u2-l3/steps/8/pairs/: Gap between MACD and the signal line
Where the EMA 12 and 26 are equal
